rationale: Round 3 closes the two reproduced Git happy-path defects: the temporary index is now tip-seeded, and materialization now uses an expected-old-tip ref update followed by a mixed reset of the real index. The requested artifact/index/interval red-on-revert legs are present, the ADR-0023 draft carve-out remains narrowly pre-epic, ADR-0025's bead-7 amendment remains fenced to the worktree-creating next claim path, and leaving ADR-0037 untouched remains correct. However, the corrected protocol's stated reset-failure recovery is not true. After update-ref advances the extant bead branch from the reviewed SHA to C, a reset failure or process death leaves the real index stale. Immediate re-invocation cannot reach the promised idempotent reset: complete's unchanged panel gate runs first and ADR-0037 section 4 blocks because the live bead ref is now C rather than reviewed_head_sha. This is exactly the dead-end recovery shape ADR-0041 section 2(i) forbids. The proposed ADR-0041 amendment also needs to state that snapshotting writes unreachable loose objects before the content gates; a gate refusal preserves refs, tracker, index, and worktree, but is not repository-byte-identical unless the snapshot uses an isolated object store. These are localized bead-6 plan corrections, not a rejection of OQ-1(a), but the plan must name a real forward-reconcile path and accurately amend the governing ADR before approval.
concrete_changes_required: Revise bead 6's materialization failure protocol so an interruption or failure after the expected-old-tip update-ref but before successful real-index refresh has a genuine bounded forward exit that is reachable despite ADR-0037's unchanged stale-SHA gate. Do not name bare re-invocation as idempotent unless pre-panel current-state reconciliation actually recognizes C and completes the pending index refresh safely.

Add the new update-ref-to-index-refresh boundary to ADR-0041 section 3's mutation-point classification and pin it with a red-on-revert failure/kill fixture: advance the ref to C, fail or interrupt before reset, invoke the documented recovery, and assert convergence without rollback, re-paneling, phantom staged deletion, or loss of interval edits.

Make the ADR-0041 amendment draft explicit about snapshot side effects. With the stated temporary index plus ordinary object database, a refused content gate may leave unreachable loose objects, so replace or qualify the existing repository-byte-identical language for this exception while preserving the precise guarantee that the bead ref/tip, tracker state, real index, and worktree are unchanged. Alternatively specify an isolated object-store mechanism that makes the stronger claim true.

findings.summary: The snapshot index is now seeded from the exact bead tip before add -A applies the named-artifact exclusion.
findings.evidence: Plan protocol step 1 and bead 6 step 1 both require read-tree <tip> before add -A, define exclusion as unchanged-at-tip, and add fixture legs (v) and (vii) proving that T and the user commit retain the artifact blob/mode and only the sync commit updates it.

findings.summary: The expected-old-tip update and mixed-reset transition are specified correctly for the happy path, but the reset-failure retry is unreachable.
findings.evidence: Protocol step 3 orders commit-tree T, update-ref refs/heads/bead/<id> C <expected-old-tip>, then reset --quiet --mixed in wtPath. That makes clean and interval-edit outcomes coherent. But complete.go's authoritative panel gate precedes materialization, and ADR-0037 section 4 blocks an extant bead ref whose live tip differs from reviewed_head_sha. Once update-ref succeeds, a failed reset followed by the promised bare re-run is therefore stale-blocked before any repair can execute, contradicting ADR-0041 section 2(i)'s genuine-forward-exit rule.

findings.summary: All three requested artifact/clean/index-split fixture legs were added, but the ADR-0041 amendment description still carries an inaccurate recovery claim and omits the snapshot's loose-object exception.
findings.evidence: Bead 6 legs (iv)-(vii) cover ordinary interval dirt, user-commit-never-touches-artifact, clean-after-materialization, and byte identity through T/user commit. The same bead calls reset failure forward-only with an idempotent re-run, which the unchanged pre-materialization panel gate prevents. Snapshot step 1 expressly writes loose objects, while the current ADR says enumerated preflight refusals leave the repository byte-identical; the amendment step does not direct the implementer to qualify that statement.

findings.summary: A crash or terminal reset error after the CAS ref advance manufactures a stale-panel dead end.
findings.evidence: State at interruption: branch ref and HEAD resolve to C, C's parent is the reviewed old tip, the real index still represents the old tip, and the worktree remains untouched. On re-run the branch still exists, so ADR-0037's missing-ref reconcile exception does not apply; reviewed_head_sha != C blocks. The plan names no pre-panel recognizer or alternative recovery that can reach the pending reset.

findings.summary: Prospective snapshotting is pre-commit, not mutation-free, under the stated object-storage mechanism.
findings.evidence: read-tree/add/write-tree through a temporary index leaves the worktree, real index, and refs untouched, but add/write-tree write blob/tree objects to the repository object database. A doc-sync or ADR-divergence refusal can therefore leave unreachable loose objects. The amended ADR should state the narrower operational invariants or isolate the temporary objects before claiming repository-byte-identical refusal behavior.

findings.summary: The remaining ADR resolutions stay conformant.
findings.evidence: OQ-2 limits filesystem authority to spec-directory-plus-conventional-branch discovery before epic creation, preserving beads as post-epic authority under ADR-0023. ADR Fitness fences ADR-0025's entangleable-dirt clarification to the worktree-creating next claim path. OQ-1(a) preserves ADR-0037's panel-before-tip-mutation ordering and stale-SHA decision, so ADR-0037 and internal/panel correctly remain untouched.
